text:
Maya: customer reported p95 spikes and a bunch of 502s from the rerank endpoint under sustained load (~1.2k QPS). says it started around 09:10 UTC after a marketing burst. sending logs and their sample payload.
Evan: can you paste the sample request here and the exact timestamps of the 502s? also which model variant are they hitting? @priya fyi.
Maya: sample payload below, they send ~100 candidates per call, batch_size=64 in client. model: rerank-v2-medium. timestamps: spikes 09:10:12 - 09:12:05 UTC. logs attached (excerpt):

```
ERROR gateway: upstream timeout id=req-8a7f path=/v1/rerank status=502 backend=reranker-03 timeout=15s attempts=3
WARN runtime: queued batch overflow size=64 inflight=128
```

Evan: looks like gateway hit upstream timeout after retries. are we seeing backend 5xx or OOMs? can infra-bot show pod restarts and tail of runtime logs for those timestamps?
infra-bot: alert: rerank-p95 > 800ms in us-east-1 from 2024-07-21T09:09:50Z to 2024-07-21T09:13:00Z. pods: reranker-01..04. No pod restarts in last 24h. Average CPU 92% on reranker-03 during spike.
Priya: seeing increased GC pause metrics on reranker-03 around 09:10. heap growth correlates with candidate count. quota check: each request had candidates=100, tokens per candidate avg=24. effective tokens per request ~= 2400, so batching pushing sequence memory.
Evan: that explains long tail. limits: we have retry policy with 3 attempts and gateway upstream timeout=15s. client-side batch_size=64 means runtime is forming big batches; with high inflight queries we saturate kernel and cause latency amplification.
Maya: customer is on Dedicated dev tier; they expected retries to handle transient 5xx but got gateway timeouts instead. They want repro steps so they can throttle client.
Aaron: short mitigation we applied: lowered max inflight for rerank-v2-medium on that pool to 96 and temporarily reduced default retry attempts to 1 for rerank route. pushed 09:20 UTC.
Priya: also activated per-request candidate cap at the gateway (enforce max_candidates=50) and enabled prefix KV cache bypass. so new requests get 400 if >50. threshold will reduce memory blowouts.
Evan: next steps: collect full perf trace for a representative request (include kv-cache hit flags, kernel timings). @Maya can you get the customer's request_id header for a failing run?
Maya: got one: X-Request-ID: acme-req-20240721-091011. sending trace link once infra finishes aggregation.
infra-bot: trace ready: https://traces.internal/rerank/acme-req-20240721-091011
Evan: trace shows long time in "prefill_kv" and "attention_kv_update" kernels; batching queue wait 420ms. backend compute time ~1.1s but queue adds heavy tail. consistent with queue amplification.
Priya: recommended config changes: smaller batch_target for rerank (32), tighter queue latency SLO (p95 target 150ms), and candidate limit enforcement + early reject. Also consider quantized model variant for high-throughput customers.
Maya: told customer we applied temporary caps and will follow up with long-term tuning. they asked for repro steps to simulate: 1) 100 candidates/request 2) steady 1k QPS 3) batch_size client 64 4) model rerank-v2-medium 5) observe p95 and gateway 502s.
Aaron: scheduled a 30-min follow-up postmortem with eng-runtime + eng-sre + support Monday 10:00am PT. will include replay from load test we will run today.
Evan: for the load test, include variations: candidate counts [20,50,100], batch_target [16,32,64], concurrency sweep, and kernel prof. will add test harness script in #eng-runtime.
Maya: customer satisfied with mitigation for now, asked for ETA on permanent fix. told them we'll share postmortem and tuning plan after tests. :thumbsup:
Priya: adding note: we should also audit retry behaviour for rerank specifically — retries here worsen queues when backend is overloaded. consider 429->backoff vs 5xx immediate fail for large requests.
Evan: agree. logging action items here: 1) run replay and produce perf matrix, 2) tune batch_target & queue SLO, 3) add candidate hard cap at gateway, 4) revisit retry policy, 5) write KB for customers on recommended client settings. closing thread after postmortem scheduled.
Maya: thanks all, closing the loop. :lock:
